name: Medicine-Ball Straight-Leg Sit-Up
definition: A loaded straight-leg sit-up performed with one medicine ball held firmly against the chest. Both legs stay extended and press against the floor while the torso lowers slowly with a slight upper-back curl held as posture, then returns to upright sitting through hip flexion. The abdominal wall resists further spinal extension as the torso lowers; the source does not establish dynamic spinal flexion as the repetition driver. The Boxing Science exercise-library fixture owns the chest-held implement, straight legs, slow descent, and four-to-five-second repetition. Abdominal and hip-flexor roles combine that fixture with broader sit-up evidence; upper-limb and grip roles are bounded anatomy-and-mechanics inferences rather than exact-fixture recruitment measurements. Straight-arm loaded sit-ups, bodyweight sit-ups, bent-knee or anchored sit-ups, V-ups, throws, rotations, and kipping repetitions remain outside this family.

variantAxes.description: Both legs remain straight and together against the floor.
The feet are not held by a person or object.
A slight upper-back curl is held as posture while the torso lowers and rises; it is not authored as the dynamic driver.
Hip extension lowers the torso and hip flexion returns it to sitting.
The repetition returns to the upright sit-up position.
One medicine ball remains held tightly against the chest.
Log the complete medicine ball once.
The source prescribes a controlled four-to-five-second repetition.

execution.startingPosition: Sit upright with both legs straight and together, feet unanchored, and one medicine ball held tightly against the chest. Log the ball's full mass once.
execution.movement: Lower the torso slowly while keeping tension against the ball and maintaining a slight curl through the upper back.
execution.endpoint: Reach the lowest controlled position that preserves the straight-leg fixture and secure chest hold.
execution.returnPhase: Flex at the hips to return slowly to upright sitting while preserving the slight upper-back curl and pressing the straight legs against the floor; complete the full repetition in about four to five seconds.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep both knees straight and avoid rotating, throwing, or pressing the ball away from the chest.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the legs together, feet unanchored, and the ball held firmly against the chest throughout.
disqualifyingCompensations: Reaching the ball overhead changes the fixture to a straight-arm loaded sit-up.
Bending or anchoring the legs changes the reviewed setup.
Swinging or throwing the ball uses momentum outside the controlled repetition.
